A1.justification: Both 42-page PDFs present the same AdaDetectGPT research, including Appendices A–G. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v4 reports original detection experiments and adversarial evaluations in Section 4, plus runtime, sensitivity, and distribution-shift results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–3 and supplementary experiments in Appendices D, F, and G.

M1.justification: The witness statistic, normal-quantile threshold, B-spline learning procedure, and black-box extension in Section 3 and Appendix C are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same datasets and scenarios, including SQuAD, WritingPrompts, XSum, Yelp, Essay, and PubMed adversarial evaluations. The added mention of unobserved prompts concerns cited research, not new experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3, S7, S8, and S11 and the sensitivity plots. Neither newly cited work is added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same sample counts, prompting procedures, separation of training and test datasets, AUC metric, model configurations, and adversarial evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The adversarial evaluations, normality checks, training-size and B-spline sensitivity analyses, distribution-shift tests, and sampling-temperature analysis are unchanged in Table 3 and Appendices D, F, and G.

E5.justification: Variance summaries in Table S5 and KS/SW tests in Table S6 are unchanged. No seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and findings remain unchanged across Tables 1–3 and S5–S11 and the associated figures, including benchmark accuracy, robustness, runtime, and sensitivity results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, and proofs in Section 3 and Appendices B–E are unchanged. The punctuation edit after the coefficient formula in Appendix C does not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive witness learning, statistical guarantees, and detection performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same limitations concerning white-box guarantees and mismatches between sampling and model distributions.

D1.justification: Implementation details, model precision, generation prompts, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, and code-access information remain unchanged, including Appendix C.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds Zhou et al. (2026a), Learn-to-distance: Distance learning for detecting LLM-generated text, for unobserved prompts, and Zhou et al. (2026b), Detecting LLM-generated text with performance guarantees, for statistical inference. Both receive bibliography entries; broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Edits expand one related-work passage, correct citation parentheses, change a comma to a period after the Appendix C coefficient formula, and update the version/date stamp. Section organization and the remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: Minor layout reflow shifts existing text and displays, including Figure 4 on page 7 and Tables 2–3 on page 10. No figure or table is added, removed, or redesigned.

improvement.justification: The two new citations slightly broaden the related-work list but provide no substantive new comparison or explanation. With methods, theory, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged, the citation, punctuation, and layout edits do not materially change overall paper quality.
